==English== {{wp|AT}} ===Pronunciation=== * {{a|en|strong form}}: ** {{IPA|en|/æt/|[æʔ]}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-at.ogg|a=US}} ** {{rhymes|en|æt|s=1}} * {{a|en|weak form}}: ** {{IPA|en|/ət/}} ** {{IPA|en|/ɪt/|a=Northumbria}} ** {{hmp|en|it}} * {{hyph|en|at}} * {{hmp|en|@}} ===Etymology 1=== {{etymon|en|id=on|:inh|enm:at|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|at}}, from {{inh|en|ang|æt|t=at, near, by, toward}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*at}}, from {{inh|en|gem-pro|*at|t=at, near, to}}, from {{inh|en|ine-pro|*h₂éd|t=near, at}}. Cognate with {{cog|sco|at|t=at}}, {{cog|frr|äät}}, {{m|frr|äit}}, {{m|frr|et}}, {{m|frr|it|t=at}}, {{cog|da|at|t=to}}, {{cog|sv|åt|t=for, toward}}, {{cog|no|åt|t=to}}, {{cog|fo|at|t=at, to, toward}}, {{cog|is|að|t=to, towards}}, {{cog|got|𐌰𐍄|t=at}}, {{cog|la|ad|t=to, near}}. ====Preposition==== {{en-head|prep}} # [[in|In]], [[near]], or in the general vicinity of (a particular [[place]]). #: {{ux|en|Caesar was '''at''' Rome.}} #: {{ux|en|A climate treaty was signed '''at''' Kyoto in 1997.}} #: {{ux|en|I was '''at''' Jim's house '''at''' the corner of Fourth Street and Vine.}} #: {{co|en|'''at''' the bottom of the page; sitting '''at''' the table; '''at''' church; '''at''' sea}} #* {{RQ:Schuster Hepaticae|volume=V|page=4|text=(''b'') sporophyte with foot reduced, the entire sporophyte enveloped by the calyptra, which is ± stipitate '''at''' the base.}} ## Attending (an educational institution). ##: {{ux|en|She's '''at''' Oxford University, studying chemistry.}} ## Working for (a company) or in (a place or situation). ##: {{ux|en|He used to be '''at''' Lehman Brothers. Now he's '''at''' Merrill Lynch.}} ##: {{ux|en|'Where does he work?' — 'I think he's still '''at''' the solicitors.'}} ## {{n-g|Indicating distance or direction relative to the speaker.}} ##: {{ux|en|Target '''at''' five miles. Prepare torpedoes.}} ##: {{ux|en|Look out! UFO '''at''' two o'clock!}} # Present or taking place during (an event). #: {{ux|en|Was he '''at''' the meeting?}} #: {{ux|en|There was a big fight '''at''' the class reunion.}} # {{senseid|en|indicating time}} {{n-g|Indicating time of occurrence, especially an instant of time, or a period of time relatively short in context or from the speaker’s perspective.}} #: {{co|en|'''at''' six o’clock; '''at''' dawn; '''at''' closing time; '''at''' the age of twelve; '''at''' night; [[at the moment|'''at''' the moment]]}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=1838|journal=The Family Magazine| passage=Lafayette was major-general in the American army '''at''' the age of 18 {{...}}}} #* {{RQ:Guardian|date=April 19, 2012|author=Josh Halliday| title=Free speech haven or lawless cesspool – can the internet be civilised?| url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/technology/2012/apr/19/free-speech-haven-lawless-cesspool| passage=Other global taboos, such as sex and suicide, manifest themselves widely online, with websites offering suicide guides and Hot XXX Action seconds away '''at''' the click of a button. The UK government will come under pressure to block access to pornographic websites this year when a committee of MPs publishes its report on protecting children online.}} #* {{RQ:Time|title=The Danger of Surrendering Your Financial Independence in a Relationship|date=April 22 2026|author=Jillian Sanders |text='''At''' 21, I moved to New York City to pursue acting. |url=https://time.com/article/2026/04/17/the-danger-of-surrendering-your-financial-independence-in-a-relationship/ |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260422181713/https://time.com/article/2026/04/17/the-danger-of-surrendering-your-financial-independence-in-a-relationship/}} ## {{lb|en|UK|Commonwealth|Ireland|especially|finance|and|law}} {{q|also '''as at'''; before dates}} [[on|On]] (a particular date). # In the [[direction#Noun|direction]] of; towards; ({{n-g|often implied to be in a [[hostile]] or [[careless]] manner}}). #: {{ux|en|Don’t just [[talk at|talk '''at''']] someone; really listen to what they have to say.}} #: {{ux|en|Stones were thrown '''at''' us, but we couldn't see who did.}} #: {{ux|en|He shouted '''at''' her.}} #: {{ux|en|She pointed '''at''' the curious animal.}} #: {{ux|en|He glanced over ('''at''' her).}} #* {{RQ:Ferguson Zollenstein|IV| passage=“My Continental prominence is improving,” I commented dryly.
Von Lindowe cut '''at''' a furze bush with his silver-mounted rattan.
“Quite so,” he said as dryly, his hand at his mustache. “I may say if your intentions were known your life would not be worth a curse.”}} # {{n-g|Indicating action bearing upon something, especially continued or repeated action.}} #: {{ux|en|Don't pick '''at''' your food!}} #: {{ux|en|My cat keeps scratching '''at''' the furniture.}} #: {{ux|en|I was working '''at''' the problem all day.}} # In response or reaction to. #: {{ux|en|'''At''' my request, they agreed to move us to another hotel.}} #: {{ux|en|He jumped '''at''' the sudden noise.}} #: {{ux|en|We laughed '''at''' the joke.}} #:
